pricing_terms: Term SOFR loans have a 0.50% floor plus a 4.00% term-loan margin or 3.50% revolving margin. Base-rate margins are 3.00% for term loans and 2.50% for revolving loans. Interest is payable at the end of each interest period and at least quarterly. The unused revolving commitment fee is 0.50% per annum, payable quarterly; letter-of-credit fees are charged at the revolving SOFR margin. Overdue principal bears an additional 2.00% over the otherwise applicable rate; overdue interest and fees bear base rate plus the applicable base-rate margin and 2.00%, to the extent permitted by law. A 1.00% repricing premium applies during the first six months after closing.
agreement_text: CREDIT AGREEMENT dated March 3, 2025, among Bracken Vale Packaging, Inc., as Borrower, its qualifying domestic subsidiaries as Guarantors, the lenders party hereto, and Summit Harbor Bank, as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent. 1. Commitments and Use. The Lenders provide a $325,000,000 USD term B facility and a $55,000,000 USD revolving facility. Term loans are advanced on the Closing Date. Revolving loans may be borrowed, repaid and reborrowed through March 3, 2031, subject to availability and a $2,000,000 minimum borrowing in $500,000 increments. The revolving facility includes a $12,000,000 letter-of-credit sublimit and a $7,500,000 swingline sublimit. Proceeds may refinance existing debt and related fees, fund permitted acquisitions, capital expenditures, working capital and general corporate purposes. The Borrower may request SOFR or base-rate loans; a borrowing request must be received by the Agent by the times specified in its borrowing procedures. 2. Yield and Fees. SOFR loans bear Term SOFR for a one-, three- or six-month interest period, subject to a 0.50% floor, plus 4.00% per annum for term loans and 3.50% for revolving loans. Base-rate margins are 3.00% and 2.50%, respectively. Interest is payable at the end of each interest period and at least quarterly. The Borrower pays a 0.50% annual fee on unused revolving commitments, payable quarterly, and letter-of-credit fees at the revolving SOFR margin. Overdue principal bears the otherwise applicable rate plus 2.00%; overdue interest and fees bear the base rate plus the applicable base-rate margin and 2.00%, to the extent permitted by law. 3. Repayment. The term loans mature March 3, 2032; revolving commitments terminate and revolving loans mature March 3, 2031. Term loans amortize quarterly at 1.00% per year of original principal, with the remaining balance due at maturity. Voluntary term-loan prepayments require three business days' notice for SOFR loans and are subject to accrued interest; no prepayment premium applies except a 1.00% premium for a repricing transaction during the first six months after closing. Net cash proceeds from non-permitted debt must be applied to term loans. Net proceeds of asset dispositions above $15,000,000 in a fiscal year must be applied to term loans unless reinvested in the business within 18 months. The annual excess-cash-flow sweep is 50% if first-lien net leverage exceeds 4.50:1.00, 25% if it is at or below 4.50:1.00 but above 3.50:1.00, and zero at or below 3.50:1.00. 4. Covenants. There is no quarterly financial maintenance covenant. The Borrower may incur incremental debt if, after giving pro forma effect, first-lien net leverage does not exceed 4.50:1.00, or if the debt fits within a separate $65,000,000 aggregate incremental basket; revolving commitments may be increased under those same tests and subject to lender participation rights. 5. Negative Covenants. Until payment in full and termination of commitments, the Borrower and restricted subsidiaries may not incur debt or liens, make investments or restricted payments, dispose of assets, merge, or enter affiliate transactions, except as permitted. Permitted debt includes the facilities, ordinary-course obligations and incremental debt satisfying Section 4. Permitted liens include liens securing the facilities, statutory liens and purchase-money liens for equipment up to $20,000,000 outstanding. The general investment basket is $35,000,000 outstanding. Restricted payments are permitted from available builder capacity if no payment or bankruptcy default exists and first-lien net leverage after giving effect is no more than 4.00:1.00; employee equity repurchases are separately capped at $8,000,000 per fiscal year. Asset sales must be for fair value, and at least 75% of consideration must be cash, subject to specified non-cash consideration limits. Mergers are permitted if the Borrower or a restricted subsidiary survives and no default results. 6. Amendment. By written amendment dated September 12, 2025, the Required Lenders consented to increase the general investment basket from $35,000,000 to $50,000,000 outstanding. The amendment did not waive a default or alter any other covenant. Except for matters requiring every affected lender's consent, amendments and waivers require Required Lender consent. Each affected lender must consent to a reduction of its principal or interest margin, an extension of its payment date, or an increase in its commitment. 7. Events of Default. Events include failure to pay principal when due or other amounts within five business days; breach of specified negative covenants; other covenant breaches continuing 30 days after notice; materially inaccurate representations; cross-default to other indebtedness of at least $30,000,000 after applicable grace periods; bankruptcy or insolvency; final judgments exceeding $25,000,000 remaining unpaid, unbonded or unstayed for 60 days; and a change of control. On a continuing event of default, the Agent may terminate commitments and accelerate all obligations, and the Collateral Agent may exercise remedies under the security documents, subject to applicable law. 8. Reporting and Security. The Borrower must deliver quarterly and annual financial statements, annual budgets, compliance certificates, notices of default and information reasonably requested by the Agent. The Borrower and Guarantors grant liens over substantially all assets, subject to agreed exclusions. The Borrower pays reasonable documented Agent and Collateral Agent expenses and indemnifies the secured parties for covered claims, excluding losses resulting from an indemnitee's gross negligence, bad faith or willful misconduct.
events_of_default: Events of default include principal nonpayment when due; nonpayment of other amounts continuing five business days; specified negative-covenant breaches; other covenant breaches continuing 30 days after notice; materially inaccurate representations; cross-default on at least $30,000,000 of other debt after applicable grace periods; bankruptcy or insolvency; final judgments above $25,000,000 unpaid, unbonded or unstayed for 60 days; and change of control. During a continuing default, the Agent may terminate commitments and accelerate obligations, and the Collateral Agent may exercise security-document remedies, subject to applicable law.
financial_covenants: The agreement has no quarterly financial maintenance covenant. Incremental debt and revolving commitment increases are permitted if pro forma first-lien net leverage does not exceed 4.50:1.00 or if the debt fits within the separate $65,000,000 aggregate incremental basket, subject to the agreement's other conditions and lender participation rights. The leverage tiers also determine the annual excess-cash-flow sweep.
loan_facility_terms: The facilities are a $325,000,000 USD term B loan funded at closing and a $55,000,000 USD revolving facility available for revolving borrowings through March 3, 2031. The revolver has a $12,000,000 letter-of-credit sublimit and a $7,500,000 swingline sublimit. Minimum revolving borrowings are $2,000,000 in $500,000 increments. Proceeds may refinance debt and related fees, fund permitted acquisitions and capital expenditures, and support working capital and general corporate purposes. Incremental debt or commitments may be incurred under the leverage test or the separate $65,000,000 aggregate basket, subject to the stated terms and lender participation rights.
professional_summary: Bracken Vale Packaging receives a $325 million term B loan and $55 million revolving facility, with the term loan maturing in 2032 and the revolver in 2031. Floating-rate pricing includes stated SOFR floors, differentiated term and revolver margins, and unused commitment and letter-of-credit fees. The term loan has 1% annual amortization, mandatory proceeds sweeps and a leverage-tiered excess-cash-flow sweep. There is no maintenance covenant; incremental debt is governed by leverage and fixed-basket tests. A September 2025 amendment increased the investment basket to $50 million without waiving a default. Defaults include payment, covenant, cross-default, insolvency, judgment and change-of-control events, with acceleration and collateral remedies available during a continuing default.

These include purchase-money liens up to $20,000,000 outstanding, a general investment basket initially set at $35,000,000 and later amended to $50,000,000, and restricted payments from builder capacity if no payment or bankruptcy default exists and pro forma first-lien net leverage is no more than 4.00:1.00. Employee equity repurchases are capped at $8,000,000 per fiscal year. Asset sales generally require fair value and at least 75% cash consideration, subject to stated limits; qualifying mergers may proceed if the Borrower or a restricted subsidiary survives and no default results.
waivers_and_amendments: A written amendment dated September 12, 2025, with Required Lender consent increased the general investment basket from $35,000,000 to $50,000,000 outstanding. It did not waive a default or change another covenant. Other amendments and waivers generally require Required Lender consent, while each affected lender must consent to reductions in its principal or margin, extensions of its payment date, or increases in its commitment.
maturity_and_repayment_terms: Term loans mature March 3, 2032; revolving commitments terminate and revolving loans mature March 3, 2031. Term loans amortize quarterly at 1.00% per year of original principal, with the balance due at maturity. Voluntary prepayment requires three business days' notice for SOFR loans and accrued interest; no premium applies except the stated first-six-month repricing premium. Non-permitted debt proceeds must be applied to term loans. Asset-disposition proceeds above $15,000,000 per fiscal year must be applied unless reinvested within 18 months. lender_rights_and_borrower_obligations: The Borrower must provide quarterly and annual financial statements, annual budgets, compliance certificates, default notices and information reasonably requested by the Agent. The Borrower and Guarantors grant liens over substantially all assets, subject to agreed exclusions. The Borrower must pay reasonable documented Agent and Collateral Agent expenses and provide the stated indemnity, subject to exclusions for gross negligence, bad faith or willful misconduct. Lenders retain amendment and consent rights, and the Agent and Collateral Agent have the specified acceleration and collateral-enforcement rights during a continuing default.
